final_message:
I built the Nocturne landing page from `data/stars.json`. The type check passes, but I couldn't run `npm run build`: this sandbox has no `node` or `npm` (`npm: operation not permitted`). I ran the native `tsc` binary in `node_modules` instead (exit 0); the vite step is unverified. Nothing was rendered in a browser and no dev server was started.

## Final report

**What's on the page.** The hero is the sky over Lisbon at 22:00 WEST on Friday 9 October 2026, drawn from the data: 403 stars and Saturn. Zenith is at the centre, the horizon is the rim, north is at the top and east on the left, so it reads as if you're looking up at the dome. The Moon and the other planets are not drawn. The page then runs through three sections:
- **The program:** doors 21:30, first show 22:00, last show 23:30; each show is the narrated sky, then the 40-minute show.
- **In the sky:** a summary and a table of Saturn plus the ten brightest named stars, with notes on Polaris and on what is below the horizon.
- **Tickets:** 12 EUR, 8 EUR for students, booked at `/tickets`.

The footer credits the Bright Star Catalogue, the IAU WGSN names (their licence requires the credit) and JPL Horizons. Every number and claim on the page comes from the data or the brief, and the planetarium is never named.

**Files written:** `index.html`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/index.css`, `src/tokens.css`, `src/sky/sky.ts`, `src/sky/Dome.tsx`, `src/sky/useDimming.ts`, `src/sky/tokens.ts`, `MASTER.md`, `preview/thesis.html`, `preview/design-system.html`.

**Process notes:** I didn't propose bunshin, genjutsu's multi-agent pipeline for whole sites: this brief is one page. Previews are in mode A, as standalone files under `preview/`; this host has no tool to render them, so open them in a browser yourself. No dependency was installed and none is missing. There is no web font: the brief allowed no font request, so the system serif and sans are a choice, with the reason in `MASTER.md`.

### Theses (UNVALIDATED: nobody was available to approve them)
- **Visual thesis:** the page is the dome seen from the reclining seat.
  - The ground starts at dusk blue `#1a2242` and dims to dome black `#05070d`.
  - Stars are tinted from each star's B‑V colour in the data.
  - Gold `#e8c873` marks Saturn only. Torch red `#ff6b57` marks the ticket action only.
  - "Nocturne" is set in the system serif (light, roman). Every figure is system sans with tabular numbers.
  - Spacing is airy on an 8px base, with one left edge for every section. Components are flat, hairline, 2px radius.
- **First screen:** at rest it shows the 40 objects of magnitude 2.5 or brighter on dusk blue, with seven named. On wide frames the dome sits to the right of the title and button; at 375px the order is title, dome at full width, then the text and button.
- **Interaction thesis:** one motion. As you scroll through the hero (pinned from 1024×640 up), a night layer fades over the dusk ground and the fainter stars come in by magnitude, brightest first, in 8 bands of 0.25 mag from 2.5 to 4.5. It follows scroll position directly and has no duration of its own.
  - With reduced motion, the full night sky shows at once and nothing is pinned.
  - Hover is 160ms `cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)`, colour only.
  - Forbidden: twinkling, shooting stars, particles, nebula, parallax, fade-up reveals, scroll-jacking, loops.
- **Allowed patterns:** dark ground; scroll-linked dimming; pinned sticky hero; hairline rules (labels and table header only); uppercase spaced labels; tabular figures; star colour from B‑V; display serif.
- **Amendments made at the design-system step:**
  - "Nocturne" is set roman, not italic.
  - The dome is `min(80svh, 48vw)` and the two-column hero starts at 64rem, so the title fits beside the dome and everything stands whole in one pinned screen.
  - The display size is `clamp(3.5rem, 1rem+6vw, 8.5rem)`.
- **Dials:** variance 6, motion 2, density 3.
- **From the design-system lookup:** I kept dark-only mode, visible focus and the 375–1440 checks. I dropped its light navy palette, the gold call to action (gold is Saturn's), Space Grotesk/Inter, glow, and the countdown, speaker and social-proof sections.

Set aside: navy stock-starfield hero with nebula gradient; white editorial page with no sky; paper planisphere; observatory telescope. Kept: the dome seen from the reclining seat.

### Read from the code
- **First screen:** the dome from the data (`src/sky/Dome.tsx:23,42`). At rest the brightest 40 are visible because `--p` starts at 0 (`src/index.css:79`). At 1280×720 the hero is pinned, and the 576px dome plus caption fits inside 100svh (`src/index.css:148,166`).
- **Sections:** all share the left edge `--edge`.
  - The program adds the times and the two parts of a show (`App.tsx:44`).
  - The sky section adds the figures; the table is as wide as its columns, at most `--table-max` (`index.css:334`).
  - Tickets adds the prices and booking (`App.tsx:135`).
- **Narrowest frame:**
  - The hero stacks title, dome, text, then button (`index.css:103`).
  - Below 36rem each table row becomes a block, with every value under its own label (`index.css:399`).
  - The times and price rows are flex rows that fit at 375px.
- **Empty stretches:** on wide frames, the space to the right of the left-aligned sections is left empty on purpose, as the dark ground. The pinned hero's extra scroll length is never empty, because the dome stays on screen while you scroll it.
- **Colour roles:** torch red is used only on the button. Saturn gold is used only for Saturn's mark, label and table row (`Dome.tsx:62`, `index.css:379`).
- **The one motion:** `--p` is written in `useDimming.ts:21`, and the CSS reads it in `index.css:82,202`.

### Checked here, with evidence (11 checked, 0 problems found)
1. **Thesis against code: pass.**
   - Hover 160ms and easing: `tokens.css:54-55`, `index.css:33`.
   - Bands of 0.25 mag from 2.5: `sky.ts` (`REST_MAG`, `BAND_STEP`). Band opacity rule: `index.css:202`.
   - Pin: `index.css:166`.
   - Palette: `tokens.css:2-14`. Faces: `tokens.css:16-17`.
2. **Reduced motion: pass.** The scroll listener is never attached (`useDimming.ts:12`). Night layer and every band go to opacity 1, and transitions are off (`index.css:496`). The pin only applies under `no-preference` (`index.css:166`).
3. **Exit animations: nothing unmounts.** The script's one finding (`App.tsx:102`) is a fixed per-row render from the data, not a toggle.
4. **No layout-property animation: pass.** The script found nothing; only `opacity` and `background-color` change.
5. **Focus visible: pass.** `index.css:40`; the script found no removed outline.
6. **Five states on the button: pass.** Default, hover, focus, active and disabled at `index.css:21-52`. Table rows only tint on hover, because they aren't interactive.
7. **Tokens, not magic numbers: pass.** Every colour traces to a token in `tokens.css` or `sky/tokens.ts`. The star tints are mixed from the three tokens.
8. **Contrast: pass.**

   | Pair | Ratio |
   |---|---|
   | ink `#ece9e1` on night | 16.6:1 |
   | ink on dusk | 12.8:1 |
   | ink-dim `#a3a8b8` on dusk | 6.6:1 |
   | torch red on dusk | 5.5:1 |
   | button text `#05070d` on torch red | 7.2:1 |
   | button text on hover `#ff8573` | 8.5:1 |
   | button text on active `#e5523f` | 5.4:1 |
   | Saturn gold on hover tint `#0b0f1c` | 11.8:1 |
   | disabled text | 5.6:1 |

9. **Semantics: pass.**
   - The sky map is an `svg` with `role="img"` and a full `aria-label`.
   - The on-dome labels are `aria-hidden`.
   - The table has a caption and `scope` attributes.
   - The prices are a `dl`.
   - There are no clickable `div`s.
10. **Web-specific: pass.** Nothing needs an exit wrapper, and no `will-change` is used.
11. **Tells against the thesis: 0 found by the script.**
    - My manual read found nothing either: no fake product drawn in boxes, no repeated layout, no floating paragraph, steady plain tone, no monospace.
    - The known reflexes in use (dark ground, hairline rules, uppercase labels, display serif) are allowed only by the **unvalidated** thesis. They are flagged here for you to keep or drop.

Script findings that turned out not to be problems: the hover rules (their transitions are on the base rules, `index.css:33,391`) and the inline styles (static label positions in `Dome.tsx:84,96`, not animated).

### For you to run (UNVERIFIED)

| What to run | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | exits 0 (only `tsc` ran here) |
| Chrome DevTools > Performance, scrolling through the hero | no frame over 16.7ms |
| The page at 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1440 | no horizontal scroll, no clipped content, the seven dome labels don't overlap |
| The page with the OS "reduce motion" setting on | full night sky shows at once, nothing pinned |
| Where `ui-serif` falls back to Georgia (Windows, Android) | "Nocturne" still fits beside the dome at 1024px |

Modules not loaded: ui-ux-pro-max (only its `search.py` script ran; its entry file was not read)
